Say we have two tables, products and orders
Product(product_id, product_name)
Orders(order_id, product_id, order_date, amount)

-products_id is the primary key in products and the foreign key in orders


```{r}
#Establishing database connection
library(DBI)
library(RSQLite)
library(tibble)

con <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), ":memory:")

#creating ordinary R data frames
products <- data.frame(
  product_id = 1:4,
  product_name = c("Laptop", "Mouse", "Keyboard", "Monitor")
)

orders <- data.frame(
  order_id = 1:9,
  product_id = c(1, 2, 3, 1, 4, 2, 3, 4, 3),
  order_date = c("2023-01-03", "2023-01-04", "2023-01-05",
                 "2023-01-10", "2023-01-11", "2023-01-12",
                 "2023-01-18", "2023-01-19", "2023-01-20"),
  amount = c(950, 25, 70, 1050, 220, 30, 90, 180, 100)
)

#transfering R data frames into the SQL database
dbWriteTable(con, "products", products)
dbWriteTable(con, "orders", orders)

#Checking what tables exist
dbListTables(con)

```

Calculating the total sales and number of orders for each product
```{r}
dbGetQuery(con, "
           SELECT 
           p.product_id,
           p.product_name, 
           SUM(o.amount) AS total_sales,
           COUNT(*) AS n_orders
           FROM orders o -- start with orders since we want to calculate sales and count orders
           INNER JOIN products p 
           ON o.product_id = p.product_id
           GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name 
           ")
```

Now to find products whose average amount exceeds 80
```{r}
dbGetQuery(con, "
           SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, AVG(o.amount) AS avg_amount
           FROM orders o 
           INNER JOIN products p ON o.product_id = p.product_id
           GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name
           HAVING avg_amount > 80")
```


Creating a new table called weekly_orders inside the database
```{r}
dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS weekly_orders")

dbExecute(con,"
            CREATE TABLE weekly_orders AS
            SELECT strftime('%Y-%W', order_date) AS week_label, --extracts the year and week number from a date 
            COUNT(*) AS n_orders,
            SUM(amount) AS total_sales
            FROM orders
            GROUP BY strftime('%Y-%W', order_date) --group together all orders belonging to the same week 
")

#checking that the table was created
dbListTables(con)

#Retrieving the tables
weekly_orders <- as_tibble(
  dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM weekly_orders")
)

weekly_orders
```
